result:
No. Do not add Redis here.

The system has one writer, restores from SQLite, and needs no cross-host coordination. Redis adds a failure domain, an operational dependency, and a network hop without solving any current constraint. Elixir already gives you in-memory state (GenServer, ETS) inside the same process, and SQLite covers durability.

Revisit only if a real requirement appears: multiple hosts needing shared state, a second writer, or read throughput that outgrows one process.
